description: McDermott Laboratories Limited Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases. We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making. Our Global Device Development organization is an innovative, technically strong, and fully integrated team focused on delivering high-quality, safe, and effective device and combination products to meet evolving patient healthcare needs worldwide. The IT Business Analyst position will assist in pursuing solutions that address the emerging needs of the manufacturing business in Europe and provide day-to-day support to the sites. As part of the regional team the IT Business Analyst will also assist with implementing global IT projects in the region and ensure the harmonization of best practices across the European manufacturing sites. Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the IT Business Analyst will make an impact. Key responsibilities for this role include: Understand Viatris’ business, pain points, needs, and strategic plans around manufacturing area. Able to manage complex process analyses for all areas of operations within the site. Including manufacturing/packaging, quality, warehouse, and plant maintenance processes. Facilitates process to gather requirements in support of efforts led by a Solutions Leader or Project Manager. Evaluates information gathered from multiple sources, reconciles conflicts, decomposes high-level information into details, differentiates between actual and required user needs. Participates in global IT projects at a plant site, as well as in projects that are strictly local in nature. Skilled in general business analysis and validation techniques. Elicits requirements using interviews, analysis of documents, requirements workshops, surveys, site visits, business process descriptions, use cases, scenarios, and workflow analysis and other relevant techniques, e.g., Value Stream Mapping. Maintains current understanding of trends and issues in the IT industry, including current technologies in consideration by corporate IT. Provides day-to-day support related to the installed application portfolio at a site. Collaborates with other IT teams to resolve day-to-day issues, as needed, such as the Run team. Proactively connects, collaborates, and maintains communication with external and internal customers to analyze information needs and functional requirements and deliver project methodology artifacts as needed (following Viatris’ project methodology) Provides support and/or direction to project and program manager(s) in overcoming hurdles and moving projects forward by proactively mitigating open issues and project risks. Maintains consistent communication channels between all vested parties (steering committee, business sponsors, IT stakeholders, project team, etc.). Supports organization change management efforts in areas of responsibility. Acts as gate keeper/local system owner for Global applications installed at the site. Ensures GxP and SOX compliance as appropriate. Function as a coordinator between SAP end users and the IT support organization, ensuring that business needs are fully documented and understood, and assist the IT organization in prioritizing requirements, developing, and testing solutions, and delivering enhanced SAP functionality to the business. Play an active role in application integration implementations for EU sites The minimum qualifications for this role are: Must understand overly complex technology projects and concepts as they relate to high-level business objectives, and ability to present those concepts to both IT and non-IT audiences in a concise and easily understandable manner. Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) and minimum of 2 years of experience. However, a combination of experience and/or education will be taken into consideration. Functional knowledge of the following SAP operations modules: Materials Management, Warehouse Management, Production Planning and Quality Management. Ability to develop a tactical partnership with business customers. Strong understanding of highly technical custom software solutions. Ability to drive complex conceptual discussions and develop system requirements. This includes the ability to generate innovative ideas to resolve problems. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of executives, managers, and subject matter experts. Strong understanding of Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) or Manufacturing Execution System (MES) applications. Strong understanding of IT/OT applications’ System Development Life Cycle and related CSV activities. description: Come make a difference in a fast-growing, innovative, Software Product Management team that combines a scale-up atmosphere with a global industry-leading product portfolio. You'll be part of building the future of Trackunit's connected ecosystem - helping shape products that connect people, data, and machines to build a smarter construction industry. At Trackunit, we put our customers first. As a Product Manager, you'll work across teams and departments to guide software products from research and idea through to launch - connecting the customer, technical, and business worlds. You'll break down complex problems into clear, actionable steps and drive product development with focus, purpose, and measurable outcomes. This role drives Trackunit's Data Products, including the Analytics Suite and Benchmarking product. These tools sit on top of Trackunit's connected data platform and give fleet operators, operations teams, and data-driven decision-makers a way to turn machine and site data into actionable insight. Data Products are one of Trackunit's highest-leverage growth areas: the ability to surface meaningful, industry-specific analysis is what keeps customers on the platform and drives expansion. We're looking for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, brings clarity amid change, and builds strong alignment across diverse teams. If you're passionate about creating meaningful products and want to make a tangible impact in a global SaaS company - we'd love to hear from you. You will be connected to one of our offices in Denmark, Germany or the Netherlands with the possibility to work from one of the dedicated offices and remotely in a flexible capacity. What's in it for you? You'll join the Platform Pod - the team building the foundation everything else runs on. The pod's mandate is to evolve IrisX into a Platform-as-a-Service: enabling AI enabled and faster development across the ecosystem, powering data-driven value creation, and unlocking multi-sided business models at construction scale. Portals is a core pillar of that vision. A place in a hyper-growth SaaS business, with possibilities to grow internally in the company. We are moving quickly, so fasten your seat belt and prepare to adjust. Back in 2020 we were 150 employees at Trackunit and we have just passed 450 employees. International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders. We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities. We do this by touching upon your impact on our triple focus: impacting yourself, impacting teams/relations and impacting the organisation/strategy. Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We do offer you a flexible setup and believe that you best can structure how your routines look like. And once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work. Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring - we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here. Who are you ideally? You've done product management in a B2B SaaS or platform/industrial software environment. You've built products for data-intensive user personas. You know what "good" looks like for a data analyst, BI team, or data scientist, and you understand the gap between what a data platform can technically do and what users actually adopt. You're a technical PM with genuine data stack depth (i.e. databricks), close enough to engineering to challenge scope and catch tradeoffs. You think and build AI-first. You reach for AI capabilities as a default design tool — not a bolt-on — and you know how to evaluate when AI genuinely reduces friction versus when it adds noise. You've shipped or closely partnered on AI-powered product features, and you can have a substantive conversation with engineers about what's feasible, what's not, and what's worth the bet. You bring great structuring and analytical skills with the ability to implement strategic product plans and to proactively make things happen with a hands-on attitude. You're an effective communicator who knows how to work asynchronously and across time zones. You're experienced in the full product lifecycle: from backlog refinement and sprint execution to coordinating with go-to-market teams. You're adept at navigating trade-offs, bringing cross-functional clarity, and moving work forward. You bring commercial awareness and know how to define and measure progress with data and feedback loops. You're collaborative and pragmatic. Comfortable aligning when you can, and pushing forward when you can't. You focus on delivering impact, not just output, and you own what you build. Don't meet every single requirement? No worries - this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're super excited about this role but your past experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply. Primary Responsibilities Own the Data Products roadmap: Set the strategy and priorities for the Analytics Suite, Benchmarking, and the data-facing experiences built on Trackunit's connected platform. This means deciding what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut, and being able to explain the reasoning to engineering, go-to-market teams, and leadership alike. Drive end-to-end product execution: Own the build process from backlog refinement to release, working closely with Engineering and Design to deliver high-quality outcomes. Lead go-to-market efforts: Coordinate with Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to ensure launches are aligned, well-orchestrated, and supported by clear enablement. Create clarity across functions: Align teams on scope, trade-offs, and timelines, especially where regional context, dependencies, or ambiguity exist. Build effective async collaboration: Communicate clearly across time zones and stakeholders, using structured, proactive updates to keep momentum. Shape how we work: Contribute to evolving product practices, frameworks, and rituals, rather than just following what exists. Partner with Data Engineering on platform surface: Co-define what Trackunit's data platform exposes through APIs, dashboards, and developer tools, and how it's documented and made accessible to internal teams and external builders. Drive data product adoption: Work closely with Customer Success and key accounts to understand where data tools create real value, and close that loop back into discovery and prioritization. Our hiring process Don't waste your time on writing the best possible cover letter for the job. We want you to create an impact that matters, and that's not in the cover letter. Virtual meet and greet. Meet Dr. Oliver Oechslein, Senior Director of Product Management and the hiring manager for this role. Deep Dive interview focusing on past experience, product craft, and team culture. Assignment-specific interview. We want you to get an insight into some of the concrete work tasks or projects related to the role. You will be given a case to prepare prior to the interview, and at the interview, you will present the case to relevant colleagues from across Trackunit, who you’ll also work closely with in the job. If needed, throughout the process we will obtain references from former employers and do background checks for level specific, if you have not provided these yourself. Offer presentation and walk-through. We’re lucky to have you! Coming Together To Connect Construction We're committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale. We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products – it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world. The question is: Are you in?
